instructions: Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water, changing the water until it runs clear, then drain it. Put the rice in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes. Take the pot off the heat and leave the lid on until the curry is ready.
Cut the chicken into 1 1/2-inch pieces and pat them dry. Transfer them to a bowl and add 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1/4 tsp of the turmeric and 1 tsp salt. Toss and leave it while you make the masala.
Heat a dry skillet over medium-low heat. Add the dried chilies and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until they darken slightly and smell sharp. Transfer them to a plate.
In the same skillet, stir the coriander, fennel, mustard, cumin, fenugreek, peppercorns, cinnamon, cloves and star anise for 1 minute, until fragrant. Transfer them to the plate with the chilies.

Add 1 tsp of the coconut oil to the skillet. Add 5 of the garlic cloves, whole, and cook for 2 minutes, until golden. Add 1 sprig of the curry leaves and cook for 30 seconds, until crisp. Transfer both to the plate.
Add the coconut to the skillet and stir for 2 minutes, until light gold. Transfer it to a small bowl.
Let the plate cool for a minute. Grind everything on it in a spice grinder or small blender with the tamarind paste and the remaining 1/4 tsp turmeric to a coarse powder. Don't add water.
Slice the onions. Crush the ginger and the remaining 6 garlic cloves coarsely with a mortar and pestle or the flat of a knife.
Heat 2 tbsp of the coconut oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onions and cook for 5 minutes, until translucent.
Add the ginger, the crushed garlic and the remaining sprig of curry leaves. Cook for 2 minutes, until golden.
Turn the heat to medium-high and add the chicken. Cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until it is white all over.
Stir in the ground masala and 1/4 cup water. Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 8 minutes.

Uncover and turn the heat to medium. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until the oil shows around the edge and the masala clings. If it looks dry, add 2 tbsp water. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the thickest piece, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut a piece open: it's done when there's no pink and the juices run clear.
Stir in the toasted coconut and sprinkle over 1 tbsp water. Turn the heat to high and cook for 2 minutes.
Take the skillet off the heat and stir in the remaining 2 tsp coconut oil and the cilantro.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: No version of this dish with 20 or more ratings could be read, so this is a fallback. The Yummy Delights (5 from 10 votes) leads because it is the only one with a short time and a whole method: lemon and turmeric on the chicken, a roasted whole-spice masala, curry leaf and garlic fried crisp, onions, then the masala, and toasted coconut at the end. Cook with Kushi (5 from 9 votes) agrees on the coconut, chili and curry leaf base. Neither Swasthi's Recipes nor Cook with Manali (the trusted cooks for Indian) has a chicken sukka page. Boneless thighs replace bone-in, Kashmiri chilies keep the heat low, and ghee is replaced with coconut oil to keep it dairy-free; cashews in one version are left out to keep it nut-free. It needs a spice grinder or small blender.
